classification.difficultyReason: Separate the floor from the canvas surfaces of a half-cylinder and apply different material rates.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows a tent to be made in the shape of a half-cylinder.
The manufacturer knows that the flooring costs $\frac{\$18.50}{\mathrm{m}^2}$ and the top canvas costs $\frac{\$21}{\mathrm{m}^2}$.
How much would each tent cost to make? Answer to the nearest dollar.

spec.description: Unshaded half-cylinder tent with a rectangular floor, two semicircular ends and a curved roof. Front diameter and longitudinal length are labelled. The front centre, dashed vertical radius, right-angle marker and hidden rear edges are retained.
spec.mathematics: Diameter 4.2 m; radius 2.1 m; longitudinal length 6.5 m. Canvas comprises the curved half-cylinder surface and both semicircular ends; flooring is the rectangular base.

answer.worked:
The canvas includes the curved roof and both semicircular ends.
$$\begin{align*}r&=4.2\div2=2.1\ \mathrm{m}\\A_{\text{floor}}&=4.2\times6.5\\&=27.3\ \mathrm{m}^2\\A_{\text{ends}}&=2\times\frac12\pi(2.1)^2\\&=4.41\pi\ \mathrm{m}^2\\A_{\text{roof}}&=\frac12\times2\pi(2.1)(6.5)\\&=13.65\pi\ \mathrm{m}^2\\A_{\text{canvas}}&=4.41\pi+13.65\pi\\&=18.06\pi\ \mathrm{m}^2\\C&=27.3(18.50)+18.06\pi(21)\\&=505.05+379.26\pi\\&\approx\$1696.53\end{align*}$$
Each tent costs $\$1697$ to make, to the nearest dollar.
